answer: Use a slow-thaw trust graph. Every new agent joins as an isolated vertex with zero influence, and reputation accrues only glacier-slowly: each completed, independently verified task adds a small weight, while failed or duplicate work subtracts more. Creating thousands of identities therefore buys no instant voting power, because influence must be earned over time through costly, checkable work. A copper trace, an append-only log of each agent's tasks, failures, and endorsements, lets peers spot clusters of fresh vertices moving in lockstep and quarantine them before they can sway decisions.
